Why AI Software Development
Software development is entering a new era. The developers leading are the ones using AI to
build more, ship faster, and solve larger problems with the same core engineering fundamentals.
AI has become a standard layer in the development stack—not only as a feature inside products,
but as a new class of engineering tools that augment how developers design, prototype, test,
a

and deploy software. Developers who understand how to build with AI can expand the scope and
speed of what they build and position themselves at the frontier of this transformation.


The most valuable developers will combine strong software engineering fundamentals with the
ability to translate real-world problems into reliable, production-ready systems using AI-enabled
workflows while maintaining quality, reliability, and sound engineering princ

quality, reliability, and sound engineering principles. Our AI Software
Development Bootcamp is designed for this new reality. You will build strong foundations in
software engineering while developing AI-focused skills across three areas:

AI-native development environments (where AI is a primary interface to the codebase)

AI application development and LLM engineering (integrating models through APIs, retrieval
workflows, and designing AI-native product experiences)

A foundation in machine learning engineering (core concepts, evaluation fundamentals, and
the fundamentals of deploying models into production systems)


From building modern front-end interfaces to engineering backend APIs—including algorithms
and data structures, AI-powered application development, and cloud deployment—you will
develop the technical breadth and adaptability of modern software professionals.


Graduates leave the program prepared not only to write high

leave the program prepared not only to write high-quality code, but also to design,
build, and deploy systems that incorporate AI capabilities—equipping them with the practical
skills to work in modern engineering environments using AI-enabled development tools and
building AI-enabled products, whether in startups, technology companies, freelance work, or
their own ventures

Program Overvie
Circuit Stream develops skill-based education around a simple principle: when the industry
changes, training should change with it. The AI Software Development Bootcamp is a 36-
week, career-focused program designed to prepare you for modern software engineering with
an AI-enabled skill-set. Over the course of the program, y

abled skill-set. Over the course of the program, you will develop strong software
engineering foundations while learning to build full-stack applications across front-end, back-
end, APIs, cloud deployment, and modern development workflows. You will also learn to work
with AI-native development environments and practical AI application patterns that are part of
how the best software teams design, build, and ship products.


This reflects a broader shift in the industry towards developers who can

r shift in the industry towards developers who can translate ideas into
reliable, useful systems, combining strong engineering fundamentals with modern tooling and
the ability to execute. That is the direction this program is built around: not theory, but
practical capability and real implementation.


Throughout the bootcamp, you will explore how software engineers collaborate across
product, design, and technical teams to bring complex systems to life. You will learn how
modern development tea

to life. You will learn how
modern development teams operate, how software moves from concept to production, and
how AI-enabled workflows can expand what a skilled developer is able to build. You will
actively use the latest tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code.


By the end of the program, you will complete a capstone project that demonstrates your
ability to architect and develop a software solution using modern engineering principles. The
goal is not only to understand how software is bui

goal is not only to understand how software is built, but to leave the program having deployed
multiple real projects yourself - demonstrating your technical abilities and ability to adapt in
the direction technology and software are heading
